In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the access part of the network is the most latency-sensitive part of the network.

the latency in an HSPA network is highly variable, depending on the traffic type, the traffic load and the time of the day, but the overall delay is still acceptable for most applications, with some exceptions.
TCP and UDP traffic patterns have similar latencies in HSPA network, and the latency is not a limiting factor in either case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the network latency is not a problem for Online Gaming and M2M traffic, and the latency of TCP traffic is not a problem either.
the latency for emulated Online Gaming and Machine-to-Machine traffic in a High-Speed packet Access network is in the range of 100 ms and 150 ms respectively.
the network is not the bottleneck in the case of M2M and online gaming, and it is possible to achieve low latencies even with legacy networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve low latency for M2M traffic, the bottleneck should be shifted towards access network, while Online Gaming traffic requires low latency in the backbone.
the latency in an HSPA network is not only dependent on the radio conditions but also on the application traffic pattern and the way it is handled by the core network.
the latency of the network can be improved by optimizing the network resources and by selecting the appropriate transport protocol.
